title: fix(scripts): count a divergence snippet's lines, not its terminators
body:
Fixes #9922

## What changed

`check-upstream-port-parity --list` printed every declared divergence as `(N line(s))` with N computed as `d.ported.split('\n').length`. A snippet that ends in a newline splits into a trailing empty element that is the last line's **terminator**, not a line, so every listed snippet read one line too many — a one-line adaptation printed as two, a 100% relative error on the shortest and commonest entries.

The count now goes through a named `snippetLineCount` that pops **exactly one** trailing terminator.

## The shape of the repair, and why it is not `length - 1`

⛔ Not a blanket subtraction. A snippet that does **not** end in a newline has no phantom element, and its real last line is the one a subtraction would delete. Exactly one element is popped, which is also right for a snippet whose last line is genuinely blank (`"a\n\n"` is a line plus an empty line plus the terminator; only the terminator goes).

Deliberately **not** imported from `fileLines` in `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs`, which is the same repair over a different population (tracked files, not declared snippets). That instrument is report-only by design; this one is a blocking lint gate, and importing it would give this gate a red it cannot be responsible for. The reasoning is stated in both docblocks on purpose — what is never copied between them is an answer, and neither writes one down.

## Pinned in both places it could return, and both were seen RED first

**The helper — the gate's own `--self-test`.** Eight new rows. Six of them are red against `split('\n').length`, and the two that stay green are the controls that a blanket `length - 1` would break (the unterminated snippet keeps its real last line). Fixtures, because the pinned population cannot supply an unterminated snippet — the shape a later rewrite gets wrong is the one no tree-derived assertion can see.

**The emitter — the wiring test.** A correct counter that `list()` stopped calling would leave the self-test green and the printed listing wrong, so the new wiring case drives the real `--list` and checks each printed size against the snippet stored in the pin. Relational, so it survives every re-sync: it asserts an *agreement*, never a copied count, keeping that file's standing refusal to write down a line count. It carries the control leg that gives it the power to discriminate at all — the two counters differ only on a terminated snippet, so with none in the pin the test would be green on the very defect it exists for.

### Reverse verification (run from the committed fix, restored and verified byte-identical)

Mutating `snippetLineCount` back to `return text.split('\n').length` — the mutation proved on disk by blob hash, not by an editor's exit code:

```
=== LEG A: gate self-test under the mutation ===
selftest EXIT=1
  ✗ a one-line terminated snippet is ONE line, not two
  ✗ …and a two-line one is two
  ✗ …matching `wc -l`, which counts terminators and not the text after the last one
  ✗ a snippet ending in a BLANK line keeps that blank line
  ✗ a bare terminator is one (empty) line
  ✗ an empty snippet is zero lines
✗ check-upstream-port-parity self-test: 6 of 66 case(s) failed.

=== LEG B: wiring test (emitter) under the mutation ===
vitest EXIT=1
     × `--list` publishes each divergence at its real size, not one more (objectui#9922)
AssertionError: expected { …(2) } to deeply equal { …(2) }
-   "printed": "1",
+   "printed": "2",
```

(The second failing test in leg B is `its self-test passes` — the child exits 1 under the mutation. Expected, and it is the same defect reaching the suite by a second route.)

Restore was `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` and is certified by blob hash equality with `HEAD`, with `git diff HEAD` empty for the target — not by the exit code of the restore.

### Observable before / after, on the shipped pin

```
- default-sweep-repo (2 line(s), 1 match(es) in the ported copy)      # before
- default-sweep-repo (1 line(s), 1 match(es) in the ported copy)      # after
```

That divergence is the single line `export const DEFAULT_SWEEP_REPO = 'objectstack-ai/objectui';`.

## Falsifiable zone — every item ABSENT, measured on this branch

- **A consumer of the printed `(N line(s))` count** — none. `--list` is reachable only through the script's own `argv` branch: it is not in any `package.json` alias, not in `lint.yml` (which runs the bare gate and `--self-test`), and not in any test or doc. `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` describes the gate and quotes no count from it. ⇒ this moves a display string only, exactly as the card claims.
- **A divergence snippet that does not end in a newline** — none. Re-measured on `main` = `272a53066`: 11 `files[]`, **113** divergences with a string `ported`, **113** newline-terminated, **38** single-line ones that were printing `2 line(s)`. Which is why the unterminated case is carried as a fixture rather than left to the tree.
- **A second site in this file publishing a snippet length** — none. Every other `.length` in the file is an array cardinality (`pin.files`, `entry.divergences`, `problems`, `candidates`, `reasons`) or the `indexOf` stride in `countOccurrences`; `countOccurrencesSafe` reports occurrences, not size.
- **A reason the current count was intentional** — none. No comment, no ADR (`docs/adr/**` does not mention this gate), and no test pinning a length: the wiring test's header explicitly refuses to assert any line count.

## Verification

- `node scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs --self-test` — 66 cases pass
- `node scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs` — 11 ported file(s) at parity
- `vitest run scripts/__tests__/upstream-port-parity-wiring.test.ts` — 13 passed
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:entry-guard`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:comment-mask-corpus` — all exit 0
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on both changed files, and `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json --noEmit` — exit 0
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on all three paths — NOT GOVERNED
- Changeset: `check-changeset-presence` verdict is *"no changeset is owed"*; an empty-frontmatter declaration is included anyway, which is this repo's first-class way of saying "no package is released".

## Acceptance notes

⚠️ Turned back rather than widened, per the card's turn-back clause — **not filed, reported here**: `scripts/shadcn-sync.js` computes `localLines` and `shadcnLines` and places both on the object `checkComponent` returns, and **nothing ever reads them**. Re-verified on this branch: those two names have exactly four occurrences tree-wide, all inside that file (the two computations and the two properties), and the result object is consumed only by named property access (`.status`, `.name`, `.message`, `.missingPatches`, `.unappliablePatches`, `.documented`) — no spread, no `JSON.stringify` of a result, no key iteration over one, so no dynamic route reaches them either. The three line counts that file *prints* all read `localOnlyLines()` array lengths, not these. ⇒ triage's candidate third carrier is confirmed **not** a carrier: the off-by-one has nowhere to surface. Two computed-and-never-read properties are a separate question and not this card's.
